about: Every namespace, call, and member a Decay script may name, derived from the host surface the analyzer and the runtime share, with a description of each and the names of each call's parameters. docs/scripting.md explains the design behind them.

globals.description: What the player means rather than what they pressed: the input actions the scene declares, such as `"jump"` or `"move"`, each bound to keys, buttons and sticks that can be changed while the game runs. A binding is written as text: `"key.Space"`, two sources for an axis (`"key.A/key.D"`), or four for a direction (`"key.W/key.S/key.A/key.D"`). A name the scene does not declare is an error.
globals.name: Action

globals.description: Which block in a 3D block world the mouse or finger is pointing at, for building and digging games.
globals.name: Aim

globals.description: Playing an object's animations, such as walk or jump, set up for it in the scene.
globals.name: Animation

globals.description: Playing sound effects and music. Every sound goes through a bus — `"effects"`, `"music"`, or any other name — and every bus through `"master"`, so a settings screen can turn each down.
globals.name: Audio

globals.description: The game's camera: sizing an orthographic view and changing engine-owned follow, confinement, and shake behavior.
globals.name: Camera

globals.description: Particle effects, such as sparks and explosions. The particles are only drawn; they are not objects and nothing can touch them.
globals.name: Effects

globals.description: Numbers stored under names that every script can read and write, such as a score. Declaring them with `state` is safer, because a misspelt name then becomes an error.
globals.name: Game

globals.description: Game controllers. Each player gets a number from 1 to 8 when they press a button on their controller; 0 means any controller.
globals.name: Gamepad

globals.description: What the player did with the mouse or a finger: a tap, a hold, a drag or a pinch. Works the same for both.
globals.name: Gesture

globals.description: Grids of tiles, flat or stacked in layers like building blocks: what each cell holds, where objects stand on them, and paths across them.
globals.name: Grid

globals.description: The keyboard. Keys are named by position, such as `"W"`, `"ArrowLeft"` or `"Space"`, so controls work on any keyboard layout.
globals.name: Input

globals.description: The number π (3.14159…): half a full turn when measuring angles in radians.
globals.name: PI

globals.description: 2D physics: moving objects with speed and pushes, and finding out what this script's object bumped into.
globals.name: Physics

globals.description: The mouse, or a finger on a touch screen, handled the same way so one game works on both.
globals.name: Pointer

globals.description: Reading settings from a profile, a data file shared across a project, such as a weapon's damage and fire rate.
globals.name: Profiles

globals.description: Random numbers. The same seed always gives the same numbers, so a run can be replayed.
globals.name: Random

globals.description: Saving progress between play sessions: numbers and true/false values stored under names, such as a best score.
globals.name: Save

globals.description: Scenes are a game's separate places or screens, such as a menu, a level or a shop. This asks which one is playing and moves to another.
globals.name: Scene

globals.description: Playing an object's sequences: choreography set up for it in the scene's Timeline, such as a title sliding in or a door opening, with named cues along the way.
globals.name: Sequence

globals.description: A virtual joystick for touch screens: wherever a thumb lands becomes the centre, and dragging from there steers.
globals.name: Stick

globals.description: The number τ (6.28318…), which is 2π: one full turn when measuring angles in radians.
globals.name: TAU

globals.description: Time in the game. A game runs as a series of frames, many times a second.
globals.name: Time

globals.description: Every finger on a touch screen, numbered from 0, for games that need more than one finger.
globals.name: Touch

globals.description: Creates automatically playing gameplay tweens owned by the calling script. Copies alias playback state. Advance occurs before the owner's subsequent updates using script delta. No automatic property binding. Curves: linear, ease, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out. Finite endpoints and finite non-negative duration are required; zero duration completes immediately. Maximum 8192 retained handles per runner; dispose unused handles.
globals.name: Tween

globals.description: The interface drawn over the game: changing text and bars, and checking buttons and sliders.
globals.name: Ui

globals.description: The area of the screen the game is drawn in.
globals.name: Viewport

globals.description: Finding, creating and removing the objects in a game. Every object in a scene (a player, an enemy, a button) is an entity.
globals.name: World

globals.description: The number without its minus sign: `abs(-3.0)` is `3`. Useful for distances and differences where only the size matters.
globals.name: abs

globals.description: The angle pointing from the origin towards the point (x, y), in radians. Use it to turn something to face a direction: `atan2(dy, dx)`.
globals.name: atan2

globals.description: Rounds up to a whole number: `ceil(2.1)` is `3`.
globals.name: ceil

globals.description: Keeps a number between a lowest and a highest value: `clamp(hp, 0.0, 100.0)` never goes below 0 or above 100.
globals.name: clamp

globals.description: The cosine of an angle in radians. With `sin`, turns an angle into a direction: `Vec2(cos(a), sin(a))`.
globals.name: cos

globals.description: The number e raised to a power. Mostly used for smooth movement that looks the same at any frame rate: `1.0 - exp(-speed * dt)`.
globals.name: exp

globals.description: Rounds down to a whole number: `floor(2.9)` is `2`.
globals.name: floor

globals.description: Blends between two numbers: `t` of 0 gives `a`, 1 gives `b`, and 0.5 gives halfway. Used for smooth movement and fades.
globals.name: lerp

globals.description: The larger of two numbers.
globals.name: max

globals.description: The smaller of two numbers.
globals.name: min

globals.description: Writes a message to the log, for checking what a script is doing. Accepts any value; combine text and values with `+`: `print("hp " + hp)`.
globals.name: print

globals.description: Rounds to the nearest whole number: `round(2.5)` is `3` and `round(-2.5)` is `-3`.
globals.name: round

globals.description: Whether a number is negative, zero or positive, as -1, 0 or 1. Handy for "which way is this moving?".
globals.name: sign

globals.description: The sine of an angle in radians. Good for bobbing and waving motion: `sin(Time.elapsed)`.
globals.name: sin

globals.description: The square root of a number.
globals.name: sqrt

this.description: The object in the game this script is attached to. Pass it to calls that act on an object, such as `World.despawn(this.entity)`.
this.name: entity

this.description: The drawn shape on this script's object, if it has one: its colours, outline and how much of it is drawn.
this.name: shape

this.description: The image (sprite) on this script's object, if it has one: its colour and drawing order.
this.name: sprite

this.description: Where this script's object is, how it is turned and how big it is. Change it to move the object.
this.name: transform

this.description: The on-screen interface image on this script's object, if it has one: its colour and drawing order.
this.name: ui_image

members.description: An axis action's value, from -1 to 1.
members.name: axis

members.description: What an action is bound to now, as a list of binding texts.
members.name: bindings

members.name: held

members.name: last_pressed

members.name: pressed

members.description: Whether an action stopped this frame.
members.name: released

members.description: A direction action's value, as a Vec2 with right and up positive.
members.name: vector

members.description: The name of the animation an object is playing.
members.name: clip

members.description: Which picture of its animation an object is showing, counting from the start of the animation.
members.name: frame

members.description: Whether an animation that plays once, such as an attack, has finished.

types.description: Playing sound effects and music. Every sound goes through a bus — `"effects"`, `"music"`, or any other name — and every bus through `"master"`, so a settings screen can turn each down.

members.description: Plays a sound over and over through a bus you name.

members.description: Pauses every sound that is playing.

members.description: Plays a sound once, at a volume from 0 (silent) to 1 (full), through the `"effects"` bus.

members.description: Plays a sound once through a bus you name.
members.name: play_on

members.description: Continues every paused sound.

members.description: Stops every sound that is playing.
members.name: stop_all

members.description: A bus's volume as last set, or 1 for one never set.

types.description: The game's camera: sizing an orthographic view and changing engine-owned follow, confinement, and shake behavior.

members.description: Adds impact trauma to the authored behavior camera. Bigger amounts shake harder, up to 1, and the authored shake fades by itself.
members.name: add_trauma

members.description: Confines the authored behavior camera to the given world-space rectangle.
members.name: bounds

members.description: Removes runtime confinement from the authored behavior camera.
members.name: clear_bounds

members.description: Stops the authored behavior camera following a target.
members.name: clear_follow

members.description: Sets the follow dead-zone size for the authored behavior camera.
members.name: dead_zone

members.description: Makes the authored behavior camera follow an entity at runtime.
members.name: follow

members.description: Sets the world-space offset from the follow target used by the authored behavior camera.
members.name: follow_offset

members.description: Shakes the authored behavior camera at least this hard, up to 1: a smaller impact while a bigger one is still shaking changes nothing, so many small hits in a frame do not add up to the biggest shake.
members.name: impact

members.description: Sets the maximum follow speed of the authored behavior camera.
members.name: max_speed

members.description: Sets an explicitly selected orthographic camera's view size to a positive finite number. Works without camera behavior and preserves clipping, fit and unknown camera fields.
members.name: orthographic_size

members.description: How far the camera view is moved sideways from where it was placed in the scene.
members.name: pan_x

members.description: How far the camera view is moved up or down from where it was placed in the scene.
members.name: pan_y

members.description: How far the camera view is moved forwards or backwards from where it was placed in the scene.
members.name: pan_z

members.description: Changes the authored behavior camera's shake strength, frequency, and trauma decay.
members.name: shake

members.description: Sets how strongly the authored behavior camera smooths its follow movement.
members.name: smoothing

types.name: ColorTween

types.description: A copied solid solver contact from the last fixed step, relative to the queried body. Sensors are excluded. Multiple points/pieces may name one entity. Sleeping contacts retain support geometry and report zero new impulses/force. Editing a snapshot does not change physics.

members.description: The other entity touching the queried body.
members.name: entity

members.description: Total world impulse divided by the fixed step's seconds, as Vec2.
members.name: force

members.description: World-space unit push direction towards the queried body, as Vec2.
members.name: normal

members.description: Nonnegative normal impulse from the last solve.
members.name: normal_impulse

members.description: World-space midpoint of the two surface anchors, as Vec2.
members.name: point

members.description: Signed friction impulse along Vec2(-normal.y, normal.x).
members.name: tangent_impulse

types.description: Particle effects, such as sparks and explosions. The particles are only drawn; they are not objects and nothing can touch them.

members.name: burst

members.description: Plays the particle burst set up on an object at another position, such as where an enemy just died.

members.description: How many particles are currently on screen.

members.description: The object's image (sprite), if it has one.
members.name: sprite

members.description: Where the object is, how it is turned and how big it is.
members.name: transform

members.description: The object's on-screen interface image, if it has one.

members.description: Stores a number under a name for any script to read.

members.description: How far the drag moved up or down this frame.

members.description: Whether a character on a grid can walk to where another object is.

members.description: Which row an object is at on a grid, with fractions between cells.

types.description: 2D physics: moving objects with speed and pushes, and finding out what this script's object bumped into.

members.description: Radians per second. Before a spawned body is built, reads its authored value or latest queued setter.
members.name: angular_velocity

members.description: Applies an immediate angular impulse to a dynamic body, independent of timestep.
members.name: apply_angular_impulse

members.description: Adds a world-space Vec2 force for the next fixed step, then clears it. Repeated calls add; requires a dynamic body.
members.name: apply_force

members.description: Gives an object a sudden push in a direction. Heavier objects move less.
members.name: apply_impulse

members.description: Applies a world-space Vec2 impulse at a world-space Vec2 point, translating and turning a dynamic body. All motion controls support the spawn window.
members.name: apply_impulse_at_point

members.description: Adds torque for the next fixed step, then clears it. Positive turns counterclockwise; requires a dynamic body.
members.name: apply_torque

members.description: Like `cast_circle`, for a box `half_size` from its centre to each edge, turned by `rotation` radians.
members.name: cast_box

members.description: Sweeps a circle from `origin` along `direction` and returns the first collider it would touch, as RayHit2d or null: a raycast with a size, for whether something fits through a gap. `point` is where they touch and `distance` how far the circle's centre travelled. Starting already overlapping gives distance 0 and normal Vec2(0, 0). The filter arguments are the raycast's.
members.name: cast_circle

members.description: The objects that started touching this script's object since the last frame, as a list.
members.name: collision_started

members.description: The objects that stopped touching this script's object since the last frame, as a list.
members.name: collision_stopped

members.description: Ties two objects together like a rope: they can come closer, but never further apart than a distance.
members.name: connect_distance

members.description: Copied Contact2d solid solver contacts from the last fixed step, ordered by other entity, point, normal and impulse. Normal points towards the queried body. Sensors are excluded; sleeping contacts report zero new impulses/force. Empty before simulation/spawn synchronization. Missing bodies/physics fail. Inactive/despawned others are omitted; removal and teleports invalidate affected snapshots.
members.name: contacts

members.description: Whether this authored 2D body uses swept solid collision. Sensors remain discrete.
members.name: continuous_collision

members.description: Authors an enabled maximum-distance joint on an existing owner with no authored 2D joint of any kind. Scoped endpoint handles become stable IDs or local prefab paths; null leaves an endpoint unbound and inactive endpoints suspend until active. Requires physics and a finite positive length. Valid before bodies are built; the next fixed synchronization creates the owned solver constraint. Invalid owners, references, identical endpoints, lengths or existing joints fail before mutation. Keeps other owner components and body motion; legacy connect_distance constraints remain separate.
members.name: create_distance_joint

members.description: Authors an enabled hinge on an existing owner with no authored 2D joint of any kind. Anchors are finite body-local Vec2 distances without transform scale. Angular limits and motor start disabled; set_hinge_motor can drive the new joint. Scoped handles become stable IDs or local prefab paths; null leaves an endpoint unbound and inactive targets suspend until active. Requires physics, works before bodies are built and creates its constraint at next fixed synchronization. Invalid owners, references, identical endpoints, anchors or existing joints fail before mutation. Keeps other owner components and body motion; legacy connections remain separate.
members.name: create_hinge_joint

members.description: Authors an enabled slider on an existing owner with no authored 2D joint of any kind. Finite Vec2 anchors use body-local world units without transform scale; axes must be finite unit Vec2 vectors. Bounds must be finite even when disabled; enabled lower distance cannot exceed upper distance. Motor starts disabled and set_slider_motor can configure it before synchronization. Scoped handles become stable IDs or local prefab paths; null leaves an endpoint unbound and inactive targets suspend until active. Requires physics, works before bodies are built and creates its constraint at next fixed synchronization. Invalid arguments or existing joints fail before mutation. Keeps other owner components and body motion; legacy connections remain separate.
members.name: create_slider_joint

members.description: Authors an enabled spring on an existing owner with no authored 2D joint of any kind. Finite Vec2 anchors use body-local world units without transform scale; rest length must be finite and positive, stiffness/damping finite and non-negative. Scoped handles become stable IDs or local prefab paths; null leaves an endpoint unbound and inactive targets suspend until active. Requires physics, works before bodies are built and creates its constraint at next fixed synchronization. Invalid arguments or existing joints fail before mutation. Keeps other owner components and body motion; legacy connections remain separate. Existing set_spring controls can retune the new joint before synchronization.
members.name: create_spring_joint

members.description: Ignores only one-way solid platforms for a duration in fixed simulation time. Zero cancels; a new request replaces it. Requires a dynamic body and works before a spawned body is built.
members.name: drop_through

members.description: Reads the authored enabled flag of one 2D joint owner, including before synchronization. True does not guarantee live endpoints; inactive or missing endpoints still suspend the constraint. Requires physics and exactly one valid authored joint.
members.name: joint_enabled

members.description: The mask for one collision layer the scene's physics world names, such as `"ground"`, for a query's `mask` argument. A name the world does not give is an error.
members.name: layer

members.description: The mask for several named collision layers at once, such as `["ground", "enemies"]`.
members.name: mask

members.description: Like `overlap_circle`, for a box `half_size` from its centre to each edge, turned by `rotation` radians.
members.name: overlap_box

members.description: Every object with a collider inside a circle, as a list, each once: an area check for a blast, an aura or a pickup radius. The filter arguments are the raycast's: which layers, whether trigger areas count, and one object to leave out (or null). Ignores inactive objects.
members.name: overlap_circle

members.description: The closest 2D collider hit, as RayHit2d or null. Normalizes a nonzero Vec2 direction; returns world-space point, normal and distance. The mask selects collider memberships; include_sensors opts into triggers; exclude skips all pieces of one entity (or null). Origin, direction and distance must be finite; distance non-negative; mask a whole u32. Inside hits have distance 0 and normal Vec2(0, 0). Queries synchronized geometry; ignores inactive/despawned entities. Ties prefer entity handle then piece order.
members.name: raycast

members.description: Removes the authored distance, hinge, slider or spring component from one owner; the next fixed synchronization releases its solver constraint. Keeps the owner, its other components and endpoint bodies/motion. Legacy connect_distance constraints are unaffected. Works before bodies are built or while suspended. Requires physics and exactly one valid authored joint; missing, conflicting or malformed owners fail before mutation. Later joint controls fail until a joint is authored again.
members.name: remove_joint

members.description: The objects that entered this script's trigger area since the last frame. A trigger area detects things without blocking them, like a pickup.
members.name: sensor_entered

members.description: The objects that left this script's trigger area since the last frame.
members.name: sensor_exited

members.description: Sets radians per second on a dynamic or velocity-kinematic body, respecting rotation locks.
members.name: set_angular_velocity

members.description: Enables swept solid collision on a dynamic 2D body, including before a spawned body is built. Keeps velocity and joints.
members.name: set_continuous_collision

members.description: Tunes an authored 2D maximum-distance constraint for the next fixed synchronization. Distance must be finite and positive. Works while suspended or before endpoints are built; preserves unknown fields and body motion. Requires physics and an authored distance joint.
members.name: set_distance

members.description: Selects velocity mode on an authored 2D hinge owner and sets its relative angular velocity target in radians/second and finite non-negative torque cap. Positive turns the second body counterclockwise relative to the first. Zero torque disables the motor (it coasts rather than brakes). Applied at the next fixed synchronization, including before endpoints are built; persists through rebuilds. Invalid values leave the component unchanged. Needs physics and a hinge component on the owner.
members.name: set_hinge_motor

members.description: Selects a force-based position motor on an authored hinge owner. Target is relative radians within [-pi, pi]; stiffness, damping and torque cap must be finite and non-negative. Zero torque disables drive. Requires physics; validates before mutation, preserves unknown fields and body motion, and applies at next synchronization even before bodies exist. Settings survive suspension and endpoint rebuilds. set_hinge_motor selects velocity mode again. Enabled angular limits still bound motion.
members.name: set_hinge_position_motor

members.description: Suspends or reconnects an authored distance, hinge, slider or spring at the next fixed synchronization. Keeps the owner, endpoints, settings and body motion; preserves unknown fields. Validates before mutation, including in the spawn window. Requires physics and exactly one valid authored joint.
members.name: set_joint_enabled

members.description: Retargets an authored 2D distance, hinge, slider or spring at the next fixed synchronization. Accepts entity handles in the owner's scene or runtime prefab; null clears either endpoint. Stores stable scene IDs or canonical prefab paths, never runtime handles. Inactive endpoints may be authored and suspend until active. Stale, unstable, out-of-scope or identical endpoints fail before mutation. Preserves enabled state, settings, unknown fields and body motion. Requires physics and exactly one valid authored joint; works before bodies are built.
members.name: set_joint_endpoints

members.description: Selects velocity mode on an authored 2D slider owner and sets its relative translation speed in world units/second along the first local axis, with a finite non-negative force cap. Zero force disables the drive; zero speed with positive force brakes. Validates before modifying the runtime component; applies at next fixed synchronization and survives endpoint rebuilds. Needs physics and a slider component; preserves unknown fields.
members.name: set_slider_motor

members.description: Selects a damped force-based position motor on an authored slider owner. Target is finite signed anchor separation along the first body's local axis in world units without transform scale. Stiffness, damping and force cap must be finite and non-negative. Enabled travel limits still bound motion; zero force disables drive. Requires physics; validates before mutation, preserves unknown fields/body motion and applies at next synchronization even before bodies exist. Settings survive suspension/rebuilds. set_slider_motor selects velocity mode again.
members.name: set_slider_position_motor

members.description: Tunes an authored 2D spring owner's positive rest length and non-negative force-based stiffness/damping. All values must be finite. Invalid calls leave the component unchanged; valid changes apply at the next fixed synchronization, including before endpoints are built, and survive rebuilds. Needs physics and a spring component; preserves unknown fields.
members.name: set_spring

Maximum 8192 retained handles per runner; dispose unused handles.
